name: harness-corner-smoke
description: Harness acceptance test: ideal divider + diode-connected nfet_01v8 bias. Not a comparator circuit.
claim: None -- harness self-verification, not a spec claim. Proves the PVT plumbing (vdd_val substitution, the process-corner .lib section, .temp) actually takes effect on real sky130 devices, so later records against this repo's own target-spec table (top-level README, DRAFT) can be trusted.

vdiv_ratio.description: an ideal divider is exactly vdd/2 at every PVT point -- the invariant control. If this moves, the harness is perturbing something it should not.

vdiv_abs.description: the same divider in absolute volts must track the supply (+-10% -> ~20% spread) and must NOT move with process or temperature. Proves vdd_val substitution reaches the netlist and is the only thing the supply axis changes.

vgs_nfet.description: diode-connected nfet_01v8 Vgs at a fixed 10 uA bias. The per-axis floors prove the process-corner .lib section changes between corners AND that .temp is applied -- a grid-wide floor alone would pass with either one stuck. Empirically (tt/27C/1.8V, this repo's own bootstrap run, issue #8): see sim/harness-corner-smoke/records/ for the recorded values.

notes: Harness acceptance testbench (issue #8), ported from 2AMLogic/sky130-sar-adc's identical fixture (commit b80c144efbf467a586f728726cabb25c1eb5a1f2) -- same PDK, unchanged. The per-axis sensitivity floors here are this repo's guard against a corner runner that silently simulates typical everywhere; sim/selftest.sh re-runs this testbench with --sabotage-corners (process-corner .lib section forced to tt) and requires the process-axis floor to FAIL.
